questions.history: On a fresh wrapper, call skip(5), read() on the wrapper, then read() directly from the retained delegate.
questions.prediction: Before, expect 5, EOF, and the character 5. After, expect 3, EOF, and the character 3.
questions.basis: Positions in the six distinct input characters identify exactly how many were consumed. The bound leaves the suffix starting at 3.
questions.refutation: The wrapper reports 3 yet the delegate now starts at 5, or the wrapper reads past the limit.

questions.history: Ask the one-character skip delegate to skip(1), then read() twice and once more.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should return skip count 1, characters 1 and 2, then EOF. Asking it to skip(3) instead should still leave 1 and 2 on the merge.
questions.basis: Only one character was actually skipped. The bound admits exactly two more.
questions.refutation: An early EOF, a repeated character, or an extra fourth character.

questions.history: With a new maximum of 5, mark(2) at position zero. Compare three single-character reads against skip(4) on a separately marked identical reader.
questions.prediction: The read path on both should yield 0, 1, EOF. The PR describes a matching read-ahead cap for skip, but landed source predicts a skip count of 4 and a delegate positioned at character 4.
questions.basis: The read predicate checks markedAt and readAheadLimit. The landed skip predicate uses only the global remaining count. Direct delegate read distinguishes positions 2 and 4.
questions.refutation: A merged skip count of 2 with delegate readback 2 refutes the predicted discrepancy. A count of 4 contradicts the PR’s stated mark guarantee.
